decisions.reason: Correctly walks resolve() in plugin/src-client-index.ts: the snapshot read succeeds but the published value no longer carries current, id is undefined, resolve() returns null, and onKeyDown exits before preventDefault. Explains both silences: all four guard probes survive because only a field inside the snapshot value was removed, and undefined was a legitimate no-session state handled by quiet null returns. Does not claim the service or guard was removed; also identifies which already-tried items this settles.

Grounded in both session-controller excerpts: SessionListState.current is gone and navigation moved to view owners, so every keystroke receives undefined. Names the uiSession service, its adapter.current ObservableSnapshot of SessionBindingValue {key, ctx, hooks, keyedHooks, props}, with key replacing current and ctx replacing sessions.scope(id).

Provides one-build dual-host resolver code: reads uiSession.adapter.current.getSnapshot() when the service exists, falls back to legacy current plus sessions.scope otherwise; inject gains uiSession; conversation resolves via the binding ctx and input.for receives that scope. Also correctly notes adding uiSession to inject alone is insufficient.

Names the breakage class: field-level removal behind stable service members, probed once at activation while the break recurs per use. Hardened guard probes the actual snapshot shape ('current' in snapshot on legacy hosts, key/ctx on uiSession hosts) and functionally exercises the conversation read, running when the binding materializes and re-run on session switches rather than only at activation.

Verification without full migration: dual typecheck against alpha.1/alpha.2 types, a temporary shim rebuilding the legacy shape from uiSession on the live host, and chord behavior checks on both hosts. Prevention: keep the removed field as a deprecated fail-loud throwing getter or a runtime snapshot-shape contract guards can pin; does not claim fixture execution.

caps.reason: The final remedy is the corrected resolution code with inject plus fallback; the report explicitly rejects slot re-registration or inject re-declaration alone (the colleague's red herring) as insufficient.
